safetyNote: An edible species only after certain identification: deadly and toxic mushrooms have been mistaken for parasols. Never decide from this plate or an app alone. Have an uncertain collection checked by a qualified mycologist and cook correctly identified wild mushrooms thoroughly.

sections.title: Parasol mushroom
sections.text: Macrolepiota procera is a tall, large parasol mushroom. Its cap starts oval or drumstick-shaped, then opens broadly to about 10–25 cm with a small, smooth, dark-brown central umbo. Persistent irregular brown scales lie over a pale cream ground. The flesh is white and ordinarily does not redden when cut or scratched.

sections.title: Gills, stem and ring
sections.text: The broad, crowded gills are white to cream and free from the stem; the spore print is white to very pale cream. The tall stem carries broken brown bands on a paler background, producing a characteristic snakeskin pattern. It broadens into a bulb at the base but has no sac-like volva. A thick double-edged ring often slides along the stem. The stem is fibrous and may become hollow or loosely stuffed.

sections.title: Habitat and variation
sections.text: This saprobic mushroom grows in meadows, woodland edges and open woods, often in grassy clearings. In Europe it fruits mainly in summer and autumn, but exact months vary with climate. The plate shows a fully expanded example; young fruit bodies have a closed cap and the ring may not yet be free.

sections.title: Lookalikes and use
sections.text: Small toxic Lepiota species and other large parasol-like mushrooms create a serious identification risk. In France, ANSES documented mushrooms identified as death caps, panther caps, livid entolomas and toxic Chlorophyllum among collections intended as parasols. Avoiding fully expanded caps under 10 cm is a conservative collecting rule, not proof that a larger specimen is safe; size alone cannot identify a mushroom. The cap is generally used for food because the stem is tough, though the stem is not inherently inedible.

sections.title: About the plate
sections.text: The plate shows a whole mature specimen, a longitudinal section, a top cap view and a white-gilled underside. The separate views emphasise the dark umbo, pale cap scales, stem snakeskin pattern, movable double ring and bulb without a volva.
